title: Working at Redwood — roles, career ladders, benefits, hiring & onboarding, and internal tools
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

This document is the canonical company handbook summary for employees and candidates: it explains what it's like to work at Redwood, outlines role families and career ladders, summarizes benefits and perks, describes our hiring and onboarding flow, and provides quick guides to the internal tools you will rely on in your first 90 days. This page is maintained by People Ops; use the related pages above for deeper team-level policies.

1) Working at Redwood — culture & practical expectations

- Our mission: make high-performance LLM inference accessible to every engineering team. Everyone at Redwood is expected to contribute to a product-minded, ops-oriented culture: move fast, measure impacts, and prioritize reliability for production workloads.
- Values (how we work):
  - Product-first engineering: ship iteratively with clear metrics.
  - Ownership: teams own services end-to-end (code, infra, runbooks).
  - Empathy: respect teammates, customers, and external partners.
  - Pragmatic excellence: prefer good, maintainable solutions over perfect prototypes.
- Remote-first with hub offices: Redwood is remote-first. Offices in SF and London are hubs for collaboration and hiring. Employees choose a primary work location for tax/benefits/HR processing.
- Working hours and meetings: asynchronous collaboration is encouraged; core overlap windows are 10:00–15:00 local for most teams and set by team leads.
- Expected outputs in the first 90 days:
  1. Complete onboarding checklist and security training.
  2. Deliver a small production change or runbook improvement.
  3. Participate in at least one cross-functional roadmap or planning session.

2) Roles and career ladders

This section summarizes role families and leveling philosophy. Detailed level guides live in team-specific pages and in the careers toolkit.

Role families (examples):
- Engineering: Software Engineer (SWE), Senior SWE, Staff, Principal; specializations include serving-runtime, infra, platform, and SRE.
- Product: Product Manager, Senior PM, Group PM.
- Research & Applied ML: Applied Researcher, ML Engineer.
- Design & Developer Experience: UX Designer, Developer Advocate.
- Go-to-market & Customer Success: Sales, Solutions Engineering, Customer Success Manager.
- Cross-functional: People Ops, Finance, Legal, Security.

Leveling principles:
- Expectations scale by scope, influence, and impact: individual contributors gain scope over systems and people; managers gain scope over teams and results.
- Two primary axes used in reviews: technical execution (depth) and cross-team influence (breadth).
- Promotion process: managers or ICs sponsor promotion packets (summary, impact examples, feedback) using the promotion template in the careers toolkit; panels include peers and a cross-functional reviewer.

Career ladder summary (engineers, example):
- IC-1 / SWE I: solid execution on assigned features; needs mentoring.
- IC-2 / SWE II: ships independently; owns small services or components.
- Senior / SWE III: delivers cross-service projects; mentors others; contributes to architecture.
- Staff: drives technical direction for a product area; influences multiple teams.
- Principal: company-wide technical leadership and long-term strategy.

Manager pathway:
- Eng Manager I: manager of 1–2 teams (6–10 people); responsible for delivery and growth.
- Senior Eng Manager & Director: broader org ownership, hiring plans, and cross-team coordination.

3) Benefits & perks (summary)

Health & wellness:
- Medical, dental, vision plans with employer contribution (US & UK plans vary by country).
- Mental health benefits: EAP and therapy stipend.
- Wellness stipend: monthly allowance for gym, classes, or equipment.

Compensation & equity:
- Competitive salary bands reviewed annually.
- Equity grants for full-time employees (standard vesting: 4 years with 1-year cliff unless otherwise specified in offer).
- Annual performance review cycle with merit increases and potential RSU refreshes for mid-to-senior levels.

Paid time off and leaves:
- Generous PTO policy (flexible vacation) with minimum recommended days to ensure rest.
- Parental leave: paid leave for primary and secondary caregivers; specific durations depend on local laws and country benefits.
- Sick leave and caregiving leave consistent with local regulations; additional emergency leave available on a case-by-case basis.

Career development and learning:
- Learning stipend: annual allowance for conferences, books, and courses.
- Manager coaching and mentorship program.
- Tech talks and internal learning weeks.

Work setup and equipment:
- Hardware allowance: one-time laptop stipend and refresh every 24 months.
- Home office stipend for monitors, chairs, and connectivity.
- AWS credits for experimentation in approved accounts.

Other perks:
- Commuter benefits (where applicable), commuter discounts, and office allowances.
- Team offsites, annual company kickoff, and regular social events.

4) Hiring process overview (candidate-facing & internal checklist)

Our hiring process is designed to be fast, inclusive, and transparent. Teams should follow the standard process below unless a role uses a bespoke interview loop (e.g., senior technical hires).

Stage-by-stage (typical):
1. Requisition & hiring plan: hiring manager finalizes role, level, salary band, and interview packet; People Ops posts the req and sources candidates.
2. Recruiter screen (30–45 min): role fit, background, logistics.
3. Technical/functional screen (45–60 min): coding, system design, or role-specific exercise.
4. Onsite / virtual loop (3–5 interviews): cross-functional panel including peer engineer, manager, product/pm, and hiring manager; includes cultural and work-style alignment.
5. Hiring debrief & calibration: panel submits feedback in the interview rubric; compensation and leveling are calibrated with People Ops.
6. Offer & negotiation: recruiter extends offer; People Ops approves equity and banding.
7. Background check & reference checks: initiated after offer acceptance where applicable.
8. Preboarding: equipment request, Okta/GSuite account provisioning, security training assigned.

Best practices for interviewers:
- Use the standard rubric and ask behaviorally anchored questions.
- Provide concrete, constructive feedback in the ATS within 48 hours.
- Avoid decision-by-consensus paralysis: each interviewer should make an independent recommendation.

Diversity & inclusion commitments:
- Interview panels should include diverse perspectives when possible.
- Recruiters will work with hiring managers to source diverse candidate slates.

5) Onboarding — 0 to 90 days checklist

Pre-boarding (before day 1):
- Complete paperwork, sign offer, and submit preferred hardware.
- Receive welcome email with start date, manager contact, and first-week schedule.

Day 1–7:
- HR & People Ops orientation: benefits overview, payroll setup, security training, and compliance modules.
- Team welcome: meet-and-greet, team mapping, and first 1:1 with manager to set 30/60/90 goals.
- Accounts provisioned: Okta, Google Workspace, Slack, Confluence, GitHub, and internal dashboards.

Weeks 2–4:
- Role onboarding project: small, scoped project with a mentor to ship a measurable change.
- Tech deep dives: architecture walkthroughs, runtime/service overviews, and security model briefings.
- Join recurring rituals: standups, planning, retro, and oncall rotation shadowing if applicable.

Month 2–3:
- Take ownership of a component: lead a small feature or fix.
- Performance check-in at 30 and 90 days with manager and People Ops.
- Career conversation: map potential progression and development plan.

6) Internal tools guide (quick reference)

- Identity & access: Okta is the single sign-on provider. MFA is mandatory. Request access via the internal access request form.
- Communication: Slack is primary; public channels for cross-team topics. Use RFCs and design docs on Confluence for longer-form proposals.
- Documentation: Confluence hosts official docs (this handbook). Use the page templates for PRDs, runbooks, and ADRs.
- Source control: GitHub is the canonical repo host. Follow the contributing guide, and create PRs with descriptive titles, linked issues, and at least one reviewer.
- Issue tracking and planning: Jira boards per product team. Create tickets with acceptance criteria and link PRs to tickets.
- CI/CD & deployment: our internal CD system integrates with GitHub; deploys to staging automatically on merged PRs and to prod via approved release flows. See the eng-infra runbook for pipeline details.
- Observability & incident tools: Datadog for metrics/traces, Sentry for errors, PagerDuty for oncall alerts. All incidents should follow the incident-response playbook.
- Internal console & customer-facing dashboards: Redwood Console (internal staging) is used for demo and troubleshooting—request test accounts from platform infra.

Usage & security reminders:
- All external access to customer data requires a documented business justification and approval from Security.
- Do not store secrets in Confluence or GitHub; use the approved secret manager (KMS/HSM) and follow the secret rotation policy.

7) Policies & escalation paths

- Reporting issues: for HR issues contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.example); for legal or compliance contact Legal.
- Security incidents: report to security@redwood.example and follow the incident-response playbook.
- Escalations: each team maintains an escalation tree for production incidents documented in team runbooks.

8) FAQs & common scenarios

Q: Can I work from another country?
A: Redwood supports remote work but international hires require People Ops approval due to payroll, tax, and local benefits constraints.

Q: What is the parental leave policy?
A: Parental leave is administered per local policy; reach out to People Ops for the exact entitlement for your country.

Q: How do I request training funds?
A: Submit a learning stipend request via the learning portal and get manager approval.

9) Ownership & maintenance

- Document owner: People Ops (Asha Patel).
- Maintenance cadence: review annually or when major policy changes occur.
- Change process: submit a pull request to the handbook page with proposed edits and tag People Ops and reviewers listed at the top.
